obligations.section: Recently resolved (archive — uncounted)
obligations.text: Board check-in duplicate-submit race — GUARDED 2026-09-07, RACE ACTUALLY CLOSED 2026-09-08. `checkins` has no unique constraint and `InsideController::checkin()` had no guard at all — a double-click/resubmit would both double-post the same note to the board and double-email `MAIL_OWNER` via `notifyOwner()` (which has no lock of its own). The 2026-09-07 fix added a 10-second same-member-same-body check before the insert, which closed the double-*click* case (two sequential requests) but NOT true concurrency: as a bare SELECT-then-INSERT it is not atomic, so two simultaneous posts both pass the SELECT before either INSERT commits. Measured, not assumed (scratch DB built from this repo's own `migrations/`, two OS processes released at a shared start instant): the bare version produced 2 rows AND 2 owner emails on 6 of 6 runs. Converted to the `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`-inside-a-transaction pattern — the parent `members` row is locked as the FIRST statement, before the window read and before the insert — and `notifyOwner()` now fires only for the request that actually inserted, so the loser of the race sends nothing. 0 duplicates in 20 concurrent runs. No upsert-on-UNIQUE alternative exists here and none was forced: `body` is `VARCHAR(2000)` (past InnoDB's index-length limit) and the 10s window is sliding, not a bucket, so there is no honest unique key to build — no migration, no schema change, dedup key and window semantics byte-identical. Three things were verified rather than reasoned about: (1) `SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL READ COMMITTED` is pinned on the transaction and provably takes effect through `PDO::beginTransaction()` (behavioural non-repeatable-read probe — note `@@transaction_isolation` reads the SESSION value and is useless for checking this), so the window read cannot miss a row committed by the request we queued behind, whatever the server's default isolation is; (2) making the *window read* a locking read was tried and rejected on evidence — it has no usable index (`EXPLAIN` = `type=ALL`, `key=NULL`) so `FOR UPDATE` full-scans `checkins` and blocks OTHER members' inserts, measured at a 3s lock-wait timeout; (3) the outside-the-window assertion holds — a repeat after 10s still inserts and still emails, plus mood/NULL-mood preservation and the different-body case, all green. The send deliberately stays outside the transaction: `send_mail()` is best-effort and must never roll back a check-in that already succeeded, and a stalled SMTP call must never sit holding the member row lock. `php tests/route_handler_test.php` + `php scripts/verify-operator-docs.php` green.

obligations.text: 2026-07-10: the "ride" personal-history page is RETIRED — superseded by a minimal public hub, same day it shipped. Josh saw the full rewrite (below) live for a few minutes and said "its too much personal info. I immediately felt exposed... its not the content so much as its not what I want here." Ran a swens round-table (7 lenses: atlas/lyra/link/pip/zone/vector/bundy) on "what belongs publicly on swens.net." Convergence, independent across nearly every lens: this domain is an identity anchor + credibility hub, not an autobiography; public copy must be *achievement-shaped* (what he's built, that it's real) never *plot-shaped* (what happened to him, when, to whom, for how much); a login gate is a speed bump not a vault, so deep personal/financial specifics may not belong even in `/inside`; the long scroll-narrative FORMAT itself pulls toward memoir regardless of intent — a confident single screen is the more restrained choice. Pip's sharpest point: exact age + exact real-world location + real name, published together, is a location dossier, not a bio — never let that combo recur, gated or not. Presented 3 options; Josh picked Option 1, "minimal hub" (his own word: "1"). New `home.php`: eyebrow, one H1 ("I'm Josh. I go by Swens."), one line of positioning (IT/retail/hospitality, Canada + Costa Rica, no dates/names/numbers), an email contact line, and links to `/office` and `/gate` — nothing else. No station scroll, no station art, no JS. The venture list (Crossroads/Selvatec/Maple/KillerBud, already achievement-shaped, already Josh's own words) needed no changes — it already lives in the global `site-footer.php` partial on every page, so the hub doesn't repeat it. `/assets/ride/*.svg` (six files) were orphaned by this change — removed same session by `/wrap`'s cleanup pass (`git rm`, plus the matching dead CSS in `site.css` §15). NATIONS Cannabis is no longer named anywhere on swens.net — the "intentional exception to name-discipline" note in the entry below is superseded; nothing on this domain names it now. Bundy proposed a machine-enforced deny-list (dollar-figure/legal-term/named-client regex check on all public pages, same mechanism as the cross-repo name-discipline lock) to stop this drifting back a third time — proposed, not yet built; needs Josh's go-ahead since it's a new gate, not a bug fix. Deployed live same session via `/wrap` — see the dedicated deploy Facts entry below for the procedure and final verification.

obligations.text: 2026-07-10: swens.net went live for real (interim manual layout, Josh approved: "2 for now"). Deploy MECHANISM/infrastructure described here is still accurate and reusable — only the CONTENT it served (the old "ride" home.php, entry below) is retired; see the entry above for the current content state. App code deployed to `/home/swensnet/swensnet-app/` (a sibling folder, OUTSIDE the shared `public_html` docroot — mirrors how `onshift.swens.net` already solves the same problem, docroot `public_html/onshift/public`, app code one level up). `public_html/index.php` is now a one-line shim (`require '/home/swensnet/swensnet-app/public/index.php';` — PHP's own `dirname(__DIR__)` in the real `index.php` resolves correctly from there, no other code changes needed). `public_html/.htaccess` merged: kept the cPanel-generated PHP-handler block verbatim, added the app's front-controller rewrite + security headers + `Options -Indexes` below it. Static assets (`site.css`, `/assets/ride/*.svg` incl. the new `origin.svg`) copied directly into `public_html/assets/`. Old coming-soon placeholder renamed to `_coming-soon.html.bak` (not deleted — a tracked copy also lives at `public/coming-soon.html`). Production `config.php` written directly on the server (never committed): `APP_ENV=production`, real `APP_URL`/timezone, a freshly generated `SESSION_SECRET` (different from the local-dev one), `MAIL_FROM=gate@swens.net`/`MAIL_OWNER=builtwithasmile@gmail.com` (matching local config's tested values). DB intentionally NOT configured — `config.example.php` itself still marks the DB block "Session 2 — uncomment when the engine lands," so this matches the app's own documented current-support level; no `swensnet_*` database exists for this app yet (checked via `uapi Mysql list_databases` — only `ac`/`capp`/`me`/`onshift`/`safety`/`seo` exist, `capp`/`me` are dormant leftovers, unrelated). Known consequence: `/admin` and `/inside` won't fully function without a DB (verified they fail safely — 404/302, no error/stack-trace leakage — not a security issue, just not-yet-functional; matches this session's "hold for now" on the private/keyed side). Also known: `MediaService.php` writes uploads to `APP_ROOT/public/media/`, which under this layout is NOT web-servable (app root is outside the docroot) — irrelevant today since admin uploads need the DB anyway, but whoever wires up DB support next should fix this path too, or it'll be a confusing bug once uploads start working. Verified post-deploy: swens.net serves the real page (checked actual rendered text, not just HTTP 200), assets load, and `ac./onshift./safety./seo.swens.net` all confirmed unaffected (onshift/ac redirect to their own logins as normal, both resolve 200 after redirect).
